## Summary

**REX** (Reverse Texture): Move byte to array An (screenpt) at position Ax,Ay.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `Dn→ (An,Ax.h,Ay.h*Dm)` |
| Syntax | `REX Dn,(An,Ax,Ay*Dm)` |
| Short | Move byte to array An (screenpt) at position Ax,Ay |
| Description | Usefull for 8bit screen linedrawing. Move byte Dn to screen An that has a linewidth of Dm at position Ax,Ay. Ax & Ay are seen as 16bit integer 16 bit fraction longs. Only the 16bit integer part is used. REX sets a byte in an array. TEX reads a byte from an array |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–8 | `11111110` |
| 1 | 7 | Dm |
| 1 | 6 | Dn |
| 1 | 5–3 | `110` |
| 1 | 2–0 | An |
| 2 | 15–12 | Dm |
| 2 | 11–8 | Dn |
| 2 | 7–0 | `00111111` |
| 3 | 15 | `1` |
| 3 | 14–12 | Ay |
| 3 | 11–3 | `000000001` |
| 3 | 2–0 | Ax |

### Notes

- available from core 12540
- B-registers are not allowed. Not a vector operation.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no REX. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use B registers.
- DO check the core: REX is available from core 12540.
